memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When Seth had lived 105 years, he became the father of Enosh. After he became the father of Enosh, Seth lived 807 years and had other sons and daughters. Altogether, Seth lived a total of 912 years, and then he died. - Gen 5:6-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The pattern repeats. A man is born, he has children, he lives many years, and "then he died." Seth, the son of promise through whom people began to call on the Lord's name, still could not escape it. The same three words fall like a drumbeat at the end of each life in this chapter: and then he died.

It would be easy to skip these verses as mere record-keeping. But that steady refrain is doing something for our souls. It is teaching us the seriousness of sin's wages, and the shortness of even the longest life. Nine hundred years still ended in a grave.

Scripture urges us to let this truth make us wise: "Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom" (Ps 90:12). Remembering that we will die is not morbid - it is clarifying. It helps us stop wasting our days on trifles and start investing them in what lasts.

The drumbeat of death runs through this chapter, but the gospel breaks its rhythm. Jesus said, "whoever lives by believing in me will never die" (John 11:26). For the believer, physical death is real, but it no longer has the final word. Christ has conquered the grave.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you numbering your days wisely?
- What are you living for that will outlast the grave?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me to number my days and to live wisely in the time You give me. Thank You that in Christ, death is a defeated enemy.
